newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing asks EU to approve its merger with McDonnell Douglas.
newsitem.headline: Boeing asks EU to approve its merger with McDonnell Douglas.

text.p: Boeing Co. has formally asked the European Commission to clear its proposed acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp., a commission official said Thursday.

The commission, which must review all large mergers and acquisitions that affect the European Union's market, has about a month to decide whether to clear the deal or, as is more likely, to start an in-depth probe if it is worried about its impact on competition.

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert made it abundantly clear in December, when the $13.3 billion merger was announced, that conditions could be attached to the deal if it appeared likely to strengthen Seattle-based Boeing's already strong position in Europe.

A notice will be published in the EU's Official Journal shortly saying when the request was filed with the Commission -- which is when the preliminary one-month review period will commence -- and seeking comments from interested parties.

The European Airbus Industrie consortium, the only other serious competitor left in the civil aerospace industry, and its powerful partner companies are expected to file objections about the deal, although their initial reaction reflected little concern.
Anthony Parr, European Director of British Aerospace, one of Airbus's partners, said in late December that the Boeing move could have trade implications besides the competition aspects.
Although he declined to elaborate, this was seen as potentially reigniting a dispute between the United States and Europe over subsidies paid to the industry on both sides of the Atlantic.
Airbus's other partners are Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace, Aerospatiale of France and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas.

The commission, the European Union's executive body, has the power to examine all corporate acquisitions or alliances involving companies with worldwide revenues of $5.754 billion and European revenues of $287 million each.
